title: PERF: graph search/understand re-parse the ENTIRE corpus with tree-sitter on every CLI invocation (index_symbols=true default) — 482ms on warpfs (83 files), 2.7s on tokio (807 files) vs 20.5ms/28.4ms with --no-symbols (23x/96x); persist the symbol index instead of re-building per process
reasoning:
PERF HUNT 2026-09-27 (warpfs-perf lane) — `graph search` / `graph understand` re-parse the
whole corpus with tree-sitter on EVERY CLI invocation (index_symbols=true default).

MEASUREMENTS (hyperfine --warmup 3 --runs 15 -N, release build v0.3.0-131-g9b89386, same box):

Corpus A: warpfs repo itself (83 graph files, 555 edges)
  `hilo graph search "config"`                482.0 ms ± 21.4
  `hilo graph search --no-symbols "config"`    20.5 ms ± 1.3   (23.5x)
  `hilo graph understand "parse json..."`     425.6 ms ± 16.9
  `hilo graph stats`                           36.0 ms ± 4.2   (control — already fast)

Corpus B: fresh tokio clone (807 files, 735 with edges, 7707 edges)
  `hilo graph search "runtime spawn task"`    2716 ms ± 193
  `hilo graph search --no-symbols ...`          28.4 ms ± 2.0  (95.6x)
  `hilo graph understand "task spawning runtime"` 1697 ms ± 82
  `hilo graph stats`                            39.0 ms ± 3.2   (control)

PROFILE EVIDENCE (perf record -g -F 997, /tmp/perf-tokio/perf.data):
Self-time is dominated by tree-sitter, not DuckDB/tokenization:
  ts_parser_parse 10.2%, ts_subtree_summarize_children 7.4%, ts_lex 7.2%,
  stack__iter 5.7%, ts_tree_cursor_goto_sibling 5.1%, stack_node_new 4.7%,
  ts_lexer__advance 4.0%, _int_malloc 2.8% (~65% ts_* + malloc combined).
Call graph confirms the parse enters via
  default_symbol_extractor -> extract_symbols / parse_imports (inlined)
  -> ts_parser_parse_with_options.
Path: hilo-graph/src/semantic.rs:44 default_symbol_extractor (called from
search_with_symbols, hilo-graph/src/semantic.rs:693-697 via opts.index_symbols)
-> crate::signal::extract_symbol_names_for_index -> parser tree-sitter parse.
understand() hardcodes index_symbols:true at hilo-graph/src/signal.rs:301.

ROOT CAUSE: every search/understand invocation re-parses every corpus file with
tree-sitter to build a throwaway symbol index; the process exits and pays again
next call. Cost scales with corpus size, not query size. GAP-102 deliberately
dropped the take(8) symbol truncation (correctness/recall — do NOT reintroduce).

CANDIDATE FIX DIRECTIONS for the foreman (measure each; one change at a time):
1. PERSIST the symbol index: write path->symbols to .vfs/graph/symbols.jsonl on
   `graph warm` (warm already parses every file), reuse at query time; invalidate
   via the same mtime/hash fingerprint scheme PERF-001/GAP-094 use for edges
   (.vfs/graph/.last_reconcile stamp pattern). Queries then read the index from
   disk instead of re-parsing; changed files re-extract on demand.
2. Cheaper first cut: parse ONLY files that actually appear in the fused candidate
   set or its edge neighborhood (bounded, e.g. seed_limit*4 files) instead of all
   corpus files; recall risk — needs GAP-102 recall tests re-run green.
3. Cache keyed on edges.jsonl fingerprint in-process (helps serve --mcp only, not
   the one-shot CLI — the CLI is the 480ms-2.7s case).

CONSTRAINT: keep GAP-077/GAP-102 exact-symbol recall; the fix must keep
`search url_for` finding its defining file. --no-symbols is the existing escape
hatch but the DEFAULT path is the one that must get fast.

VERIFY WITH: the exact hyperfine commands above (same build profile, same corpora)
+ `cargo test -p hilo_graph --lib` (GAP-077/GAP-102 recall tests) + the GAP-102
20-query sorted/collapse check.

reasoning: Owner ask 2026-10-03: 'understanding test coverage and links of stuff ... how many surfaces are being tested'. Today the only unit the graph knows is a FILE: `graph untested` is file_is_covered, `graph module` prints a file ratio, and stats.tested_pct is a file ratio — so 'is the MCP tool surface covered' / 'is this CLI verb covered' is unanswerable, even though hilo's entire value proposition is agent-facing surfaces. The surfaces are enumerable from code (hilo-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs tool registry, hilo-cli clap subcommand tree, hilo-ffi UniFFI exports, hilo-fuse mount ops, user.vfs.* config keys) but nothing emits them as data. GAP-113 (the aggregate wiring report) explicitly names 'a public-surface definition per module' as one of its missing pieces — this row IS that foundation; GAP-113 consumes it.
acceptance_criteria: New artifact `.vfs/graph/surfaces.jsonl` (append-only, same discipline as edges.jsonl) with one row per surface: {surface_id, kind, owner_file, owner_symbol, name, public}. kind in {cli_verb, cli_flag, mcp_tool, ffi_export, fuse_op, config_key, public_api_item}.

surface_id is content-derived and STABLE across runs (e.g. hash of kind+owner_file+owner_symbol) — it must not change when unrelated code moves, because COV-2/COV-5 and the deltas in GAP-113 key on it.

Enumeration is derived from code, never a hand-written list; a unit test asserts known counts on a fixture (at minimum: the 17 registered MCP tool names from the server's own registry, and a sample of clap verbs from hilo-cli).
`hilo graph surfaces [--json] [--kind K]` prints them; the JSON shape is stable and locked by a test.

Honest per-kind denominators: each kind reports detected vs expected (e.g. cli_verb: N subcommands parsed of N registered) so a parser that finds nothing reads as a gap, not as an empty success (the DF-WARPFS-41 / GAP-085 silent-empty class).
Own-repo run recorded in the row result with real per-kind counts.

title: P1 — COVERAGE-LINK MODEL: make the test→surface link a first-class EVIDENCED relation (evidence kind + confidence + direction), replacing today's silent import-derived file proxy that misses whole edge classes
reasoning: Owner ask 2026-10-03: 'our issue is something beyond just raw code coverage, it's the LINKS of the code coverage'. Today `tested_by` is a file→file edge inferred from imports, with no evidence field, no confidence, and no direction semantics — and the docs already had to be corrected to say it is a proxy and NOT test-suite coverage (the wording fix landed with GAP-066 lineage). Its known misses are filed separately and are all the same shape: pkg: targets (GAP-066), TS/JS local: targets (GAP-071), flat top-level modules (GAP-104), Java file-form (DF-WARPFS-37). Because the link carries no evidence, a consumer cannot tell 'this test directly imports the module' from 'this test merely shares a package', and cannot see a link at all when the inference fails — it reads as zero coverage rather than as an unknown. This row makes the link auditable.
acceptance_criteria: New artifact `.vfs/graph/coverage_links.jsonl`: one row per link {test_file, target (surface_id from COV-1 when resolvable, else module/file), evidence_kind, confidence, direction} where evidence_kind in {import, symbol_name_match, fixture_or_helper, declared_mapping, runtime_trace}.
Every emitted link carries an evidence_kind and a confidence — no link is emitted without provenance. A test that establishes no link must not silently disappear.
Layers are ADDITIVE and ordered: a later, stronger layer (runtime_trace) can raise confidence on an existing link without creating a duplicate row; one link id per (test_file, target).
`hilo graph coverage-links [--json] [--surface ID] [--unlinked]` answers both 'what tests cover this surface' and 'which surfaces have NO link at all'.

The unlinked set is reported with a per-cause breakdown (no test file imports it / inference failed for language X / target is not a modeled surface) so a false zero is distinguishable from a real gap — never a bare empty list.
A fixture proves both directions: a deliberately-linked surface reports its link with evidence, a deliberately-unlinked one reports unlinked WITH a cause.
Independence guard: existing `tested_by` edges and file-level consumers keep their current behaviour (this is additive; the new artifact is what the score consumes).

title: P1 — TEST-CLASS TAXONOMY + PER-SURFACE CLASS MIX: classify every test by CLASS and report which classes exist per surface, flagging surfaces whose only coverage is a single class (the 'right type and classes of tests' question)
reasoning: Owner ask 2026-10-03: 'know we have all the right type and classes of tests'. Today hilo's model of a test is binary: classify.rs assigns role=test (or the file is merely untested). There is no class, so a surface with 40 unit tests and zero integration/e2e/conformance coverage reads as fully covered. That is exactly the gap: the fleet has already produced real incidents where a green unit suite coexisted with an unwired production path (the GAP-112 conformance case, trouble TRBL-084), so class diversity is the signal that matters, not test count. Note the companion row GR-144 owns the same taxonomy for the HARNESS side; this row owns it for hilo's graph so it can be joined to surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit, documented classification rule (path + filename + marker/attribute) maps every test file — and every test function where discoverable — to a class in {unit, integration, e2e_process, conformance_golden, property_fuzz, chaos_fault, bench, doc_smoke}.
`hilo graph test-classes [--json]` reports: totals per class, and per-surface the set of classes that reach it (joined via COV-2 links).
A surface whose reachable classes are a single class (the common case: unit-only) is flagged `class_gap` with the missing classes named.
The rule is pinned by a test on a fixture tree that contains one test of each class, so a rule change that silently reclassifies everything fails loudly.
Honest zero: a class with zero tests reports 0 and names itself — never an absent key (the 'a NULL must carry a reason' rule).
Own-repo run recorded in the row result: the real per-class counts for this repo, plus the list of class_gap surfaces.

title: P2 — SURFACE GROUPING + ROLLUP: group surfaces into features/components (xattr-driven, with crate/module defaults) and roll coverage + class mix up to the group so 'is this GROUP covered' is one query
reasoning: Owner ask 2026-10-03: 'how to group them'. COV-1 enumerates individual surfaces and COV-3 gives per-surface class mix, but the question a human actually asks is coarser than a single function and finer than a whole repo: 'is the workspace-mount feature covered', 'is the backend sync path covered'. Nothing today expresses that grouping, so every answer has to be re-derived by hand and cannot be tracked over time. hilo already has the natural carrier for the grouping (the user.vfs.* xattr namespace, e.g. user.vfs.feature / user.vfs.component) plus a structural fallback (crate + module path), so the grouping should be data, not a query written per ask.
acceptance_criteria: A group is defined by an explicit rule with a documented precedence: (1) explicit xattr/user.vfs.feature|component, (2) crate boundary, (3) module path prefix. The chosen source per surface is recorded on the surface row, not inferred at read time.
`hilo graph rollup [--by feature|crate|module] [--json]` returns per group: member surface count, covered/uncovered counts, class mix, and the wiring numbers from GAP-113 rolled up.
Groups with no xattr grouping still resolve (structural fallback) so the report is never empty on an un-annotated repo — and the fallback used is stated in the output.
Rollup arithmetic is checked by a test: the sum of group surface counts equals the total surface count (no double-counting, no dropped surfaces).
A group can be named as a target (`hilo graph rollup --group <name>`) and answers with its own gap list (uncovered surfaces, class-gap surfaces).

title: P2 — SYMBOL-LEVEL CONNECTION + TEST AUDIT: 'every public function is reachable from an entrypoint AND has a test link' as one query, so dead/isolated/unwired surfaces are named individually rather than averaged into a percentage
reasoning:
Owner ask 2026-10-03: 'make sure all functions are connected and all functions have tests ... if we can have a way of making sure that tests cover every surface'. The graph's own primitives are file-scoped (impact/related/untested), so a public function that is defined but never called from any entrypoint — or called but never linked to a test — is invisible as an individual fact and only shows up as a diluted file-level ratio. This is the symbol-granularity complement to GAP-113 (per-module aggregate) and COV-2 (the links); it produces the named list an agent can act on.

[CROSS-REF 2026-10-03] Related to GAP-112 but NOT the same question, and both are wanted. This row audits SYMBOLS (is each public symbol reachable and tested). GAP-112 audits CAPABILITIES (does each interface consumed in production have a non-test satisfier). The reference incident trouble TRBL-084 passes this row's check and fails GAP-112: the production sinks existed, were reachable and were tested — what was missing was a *method* (the optional BatchWriter's AppendBatch) on those production types. A per-symbol audit reports healthy because there is no symbol to audit for an interface method that was never written. Land both; do not close one as a duplicate of the other. Sequencing: GAP-112 depends on conformance edges existing, which this COV family does not require — so COV-5 can proceed in parallel.
acceptance_criteria: One query (CLI + MCP) answers, per public function/surface: is it reachable from a declared entrypoint (COV-1's entrypoint surfaces), and does it carry a coverage link (COV-2). Output is the named list, not a score.

The result partitions into three explicit buckets — unreachable (no caller path from an entrypoint), unlinked (reachable, no test link), and ok — with counts per bucket, so a partial implementation reports the buckets it can prove and names the rest as unknown rather than collapsing them into 'ok'.
No silent empties: an empty bucket is reported as an explicit zero with the rule that produced it (the GAP-085 / DF-WARPFS-41 class: a success-shaped empty report is a defect, not a pass).
A fixture with one of each (an unreachable pub fn, a reachable-but-unlinked pub fn, a fully-wired one) asserts exactly one hit per bucket.
Own-repo run recorded in the row result with the real bucket counts and the top named offenders.

Wave 11 used Hilo's mapped `graph search` + `graph understand` workflow on six pinned repositories. Hilo natural-search MRR was 0.025 across all six eligible prompts (misses count as zero); the primary defining file appeared in only 2/6 outputs, at output lines 12 (Svelte keyed-each reconciliation) and 15 (Spring Boot RestClient auto-configuration). It missed the Pydantic computed-field owner (`pydantic/fields.py`), Ruff B905 rule implementation, and Deno test-name-filter declaration; the gRPC immediate-expiry Alarm owner was also absent. This is separate from the strong exact-symbol baseline (MRR 0.457 on 12 exact queries): the gap is intent-to-owner retrieval/ranking, not basic exact symbol lookup.

title: P1 — Terraform/HCL infrastructure-as-code graph support, including links from deployed resources to application surfaces such as Express services
reasoning: Owner ask 2026-10-06: add Terraform (tf) support so Hilo can understand Express and related application/infrastructure constructs together. The Wave 9 component audit already found terraform/ among the real but unrecognized deploy directories (GAP-109); that is only a directory-inventory miss, not Terraform semantic support. Hilo currently needs to treat Terraform as infrastructure with typed resources and relationships, not as opaque text or a component name. The key value is the cross-layer wiring: an Express/API service's deployment path (for example, app/service -> Terraform module -> API Gateway/load balancer/compute resource) should be navigable and its links should state their evidence rather than be guessed. This is distinct from COV-1..COV-5, which model source-code consumer surfaces and their tests; Terraform adds infrastructure surfaces and deployment edges that can join those application surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Recognize and index Terraform `.tf` and `.tf.json` files as infrastructure surfaces in inventory/component reports; unsupported syntax is surfaced as a parse/coverage gap, never silently treated as an ordinary unparsed file.

Extract typed Terraform entities for provider, module, resource, data, variable, local, and output blocks, retaining canonical addresses (including module nesting and resource instances) and source locations.

Emit typed, provenance-bearing graph relations for module sources, `depends_on`, resource/data references in expressions, variable/local references, and module input/output wiring; handle common interpolation and references without flattening them into untyped text edges.

Allow graph related/impact/understand and component rollups to traverse infrastructure and application code together. Include an integration fixture with an Express.js service and Terraform deployment resources (e.g. module plus API Gateway/load balancer and compute target) that proves the service-to-deployment path and reverse impact path.

Connect application surfaces to Terraform resources only through evidence-backed links (explicit variable/output/environment/config reference, framework/deployment convention with stated confidence, or an explicit user mapping). Ambiguous or missing links are reported as unknown/unlinked with a reason; do not infer that an Express service is deployed by a nearby Terraform resource merely because names or directories look similar.

Add parser and graph fixtures covering a root module plus nested module, provider/resource/data blocks, outputs/variables, dependencies, and a malformed/unsupported construct; assert exact node and edge sets, source locations, parse diagnostics, and zero false links.
Document supported Terraform/HCL constructs and limits; keep parsing local/static and do not require Terraform CLI, cloud credentials, provider initialization, or deployment to inspect a repo.

title: [P1] workspace sync --push/--pull/--both flags are INERT: direction only changes the header label, every run is a full two-way sync — --push downloads remote-only files, --pull uploads local-only files

Fix direction: thread SyncDirection through SyncEngine::new/plan/sync (skip the opposite hemisphere of plan items per direction), and make '↑' items impossible under --pull / '↓' items impossible under --push.

title: [P0] workspace manifest `ref: <branch>` NEVER mounts: WorktreeManager.checkout_ref resolves branch names as refs/tags/<ref> only — the doc example itself fails with 'revspec refs/tags/main not found', and the failed ensure leaves an empty ~/.hilo/worktrees/<name> dir that wedges every retry
description: Dogfood run 38 (tick warpfs-dogfood-2026-10-10-05-39-14, hilo 0.4.0 v0.3.0-343-ga996ef92, release build) drove `workspace mount` on a fresh scratch manifest (2 repos, ref: main) — the FIRST dogfood run on this surface. Both fresh-clone attempts failed identically: 'error: failed to build mount plan: Validation failed: failed to ensure worktree for repo-a: git operation failed: revspec 'refs/tags/main' not found; class=Reference (4); code=NotFound (-3)'. Root cause: hilo-core/src/worktree.rs:174-186 checkout_ref tries revparse(ref), then refs/heads/<ref>, then refs/tags/<ref> — but on a FRESH git2::Repository::clone, refs/heads/* contains ONLY the clone default branch (master here), so any repo whose default branch differs from the manifest ref (e.g. clone gives master, manifest says main) hits only the tags arm and dies. Worse: ensure() (worktree.rs:62-77) does std::fs::create_dir_all BEFORE the clone (line 72), and the failed clone leaves an EMPTY dir with no .git — every subsequent mount attempt takes the 'already cloned' path (line 63: worktree_path.join(".git").exists() is false so it retries clone... actually it re-clones into the empty dir and fails again, but list()/user tooling sees a half-state). Re-proved three times with identical output. The manifest's own doc example (hilo-core/src/workspace.rs:417-424) uses ref: main — the documented shape cannot mount a branch that is not the clone default. Fix direction: on fresh clone, resolve the requested ref against the FETCHED refs (git2 fetch of +refs/heads/* before checkout_ref, as the ensure-already-cloned path does), or clone with the ref's branch checked out (git2::build::RepoBuilder with fetch options refspec), and clean up the worktree dir when clone fails.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh-machine `hilo workspace mount` with a manifest whose repos declare `ref: <branch other than the clone default>` completes and the tree is browsable; a failed ensure leaves no ~/.hilo/worktrees/<name> residue.

title: [P1] PERF: first full traversal over the mount costs 14-20s COLD (graph pre-warmed) and 1.2-2.1s WARM vs 9ms native — ~52% of samples are std::path parsing inside readdir

Evidence, exact commands: `time find /tmp/df39mnt -name '*.rs' | wc -l` = 157 files, COLD 14.003s (first mount) / 19.87s (second mount, graph.db mtime untouched by the mount — pre-warm buys nothing); warm hyperfine --warmup 2 --runs 10 = 1.162s +/- 0.039 (single-repo mount), 2.082s +/- 0.455 after remount; native control on the same tree = 0.009s (~129x). Hot paths: hilo-fuse/src/ops.rs readdir/populate_directory. This UPDATES PERF-011 (filed 2.7-8.0s on a 5-file project; 222 files pushes cold to 20s). Fix direction: parent->children index built at populate time (kills both the O(n) .any() scan and the per-lookup full-path reparse), or an inode->PathBuf map with cached Parents.

title: [P2] SKIPPED-install-bunker: fresh-install leg UNPROVEN — ephemeral agent expired mid-build when the host clock jumped ~6 days, consuming its TTL
description: Dogfood run 45 (tick warpfs-dogfood-2026-10-13-17-25-05, second live instance; sibling instance landed run 42) attempted the ephemeral fresh-install leg on a spawned bunker-mvp agent (id 757e8e71, 8 vCPU, Ubuntu 24.04, no rust toolchain, /usr/bin/cc + g++ + make + perl present, no pkg-config/fuse3-dev). Completed steps, all evidence from $HOME/df42-i2.log inside the agent: (1) `git clone https://github.com/gethilo/hilo.git` rc=0, HEAD 5deb8880bdfa0806b39b8a98cbfb9cbdfa9ad123 — the public https clone works uncredentialed; (2) documented no-sudo bootstrap `curl https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal` rc=0 (NOTE: the README's verbatim form without -y dies in a non-interactive shell with 'Unable to run interactively' — that is a harness artifact, a real user has a TTY, so NOT filed as a product defect); (3) `cargo build --release -p hilo-cli --no-default-features --features vendored-openssl` launched and was still compiling. BUILD_RC and the `hilo --version` smoke were NEVER captured: the agent hit its 3h TTL and its home was destroyed (ssh: 'failed to look up local user bunker-757e8e71'), because the CONTROL host's clock advanced from 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-19 during this tick (bunker list shows agents stamped 2026-10-19T13:52:13Z), so a 3h TTL expired in what this session experienced as well under an hour. Installability from a fresh machine is therefore UNPROVEN for this run and must not read as a pass. Prior runs 35+36 proved a fresh-machine install PASS and run 41 proved a non-deterministic libduckdb-sys SIGABRT wall on <=4GB agents (DF-WARPFS-142) — this agent had 15.6GB total (11.0GB free), i.e. above that wall, and its build was still alive when the TTL fired, so it neither confirms nor refutes DF-142. Fix direction: none for the product; the missing capability is in the harness — the dogfood install leg needs either a TTL that scales with host-monotonic time (not wall clock) or an evidence-capture step that streams BUILD_RC and `hilo --version` back to the control host incrementally, so a leg that dies mid-build still leaves a graded result instead of an unproven gap.
acceptance: A fresh-install run on an ephemeral bunker agent captures clone rc, rustup rc, `cargo build --release -p hilo-cli --no-default-features --features vendored-openssl` rc and `hilo --version` output on the control host even if the agent is destroyed mid-run, and install_seconds is reported.

title: [P2] The daemon log lives INSIDE the mount, so it is unreadable exactly when the daemon dies — and the mountpoint is left ENOTCONN with the banner still promising 'filesystem available'
description: Dogfood run 45, re-driving the DF-WARPFS-134 fix (`--daemon` keeps child stderr, default log <mount_point>/.vfs/logs/mount-daemon.log) on the HEAD release build (build stamp 'v0.3.0-446-g5deb8880-dirty', /var/tmp/hermes-cargo-target/release/hilo). Bare project /home/kara/df42/df42-proj (git init, src/app.py + src/lib.py, `hilo init`, `hilo graph warm`: 2 edges / 1 file). Four separate `hilo mount <dir> --triggers --daemon` sessions. OBSERVED, in every session: the parent prints `Hilo mount daemonized (pid N) — filesystem available at <dir> (log: <dir>/.vfs/logs/mount-daemon.log)`, the log file is created at that default path and receives the trigger-engine startup lines (`[trigger-engine] loaded 13 triggers for mount ...`, `... watching ... 13 triggers active`) plus hilo_fuse::daemon / fuser::session INFO mount lines — i.e. the DF-134 fix itself is CONFIRMED (independent re-proof of sibling run 42's conclusion). THE GAP: once the daemon process is gone, the SAME default log path becomes unreadable, because it is served by the dead mount — every read of /home/kara/df42/df42-proj/.vfs/logs/mount-daemon.log returns `ls: unknown io error ... Os { code: 107, kind: NotConnected, message: "Transport endpoint is not connected" }`, and so does any other path under the mountpoint (`ls <dir>` -> ENOTCONN). Meanwhile the mount STILL appears in /proc/mounts / findmnt (`hilo on <dir> type fuse ro,...`), the daemon PID is gone (`ps -eo args | grep 'hilo mount'` empty), and clearing it required `umount -l <dir>` (plain `fusermount3 -u <dir>` worked only in the session where the daemon was still alive). Consequence for a real user: the banner said 'filesystem available', and after the daemon dies the tree dead-ends with a kernel errno that names neither the mount nor a log path — and the one artifact that would explain the death (the durable log the DF-134 fix added) is unreachable through the very mount that died. A log path chosen OUTSIDE the mounted tree (or a second copy under ~/.hilo/logs/) plus a liveness affordance would make the fix's own promise hold post-mortem. The cause of each daemon exit was NOT attributed by this run (harness-side process lifecycle and the run-37/DF-63 teardown-hang class are both candidates); the diagnosability gap is independent of the cause: any crash, OOM or kill reproduces it. Related: DF-WARPFS-134 (fixed, this is the completeness gap in its acceptance), DF-WARPFS-63 (daemon hangs), DF-WARPFS-32 (trigger-mount teardown leak).
acceptance: After the mount daemon exits for ANY reason, (a) the log file is still readable from a path outside the mountpoint, (b) the banner/app prints the log path in a form the user can read post-mortem, and (c) the mountpoint does not remain listed in /proc/mounts returning ENOTCONN without a message naming the dead mount; a test kills the daemon mid-session and asserts (a)-(c).

title: [P1] RECURRENCE (GAP-104 / GAP-064): a Python module in a SUBDIRECTORY imported by basename from a path-entry has no file node — `graph impact scripts/drivers/base.py` says 'no dependents' while 6 importers exist and `impact pkg:base` lists all 6; the same cause makes `graph untested` call 3 test-imported modules untested
description:
Dogfood run 46, HEAD 33ce3a24, binary /var/tmp/hermes-cargo-target/release/hilo (build stamp v0.3.0-530-g33ce3a24-dirty, built 2026-10-20T10:32:47Z), corpus fresh local clone of the task-router repo at d643ef4 (730 tracked files / 314 .py), cloned to /tmp/df46-1206/tr, warmed (8.28 s, 3337 edges / 304 files).

GROUND TRUTH (grep -rn 'from base import|import base' scripts/drivers/*.py): 5 sibling driver modules + scripts/drivers/__init__.py import it, i.e. 6 real dependents. The graph HAS the edges — 6 rows in .vfs/graph/edges.jsonl with {"to":"pkg:base","rel":"imports","provenance":"ast_exact","confidence":1.0} — and the pkg-form query `hilo graph impact pkg:base` returns all 6 at depth 1 plus 6 more at depth 2 (via pkg:drivers). So the data is present and the FILE-form query (the form a user/agent has, because they hold a path) cannot join its own file node to the pkg node its importers target. Contrast the flat module scripts/router_server.py on the same corpus: file-form impact correctly returns 41 dependents (scope=crate, via pkg:router_server) — so the failure is specific to a module whose import site is the SUBDIRECTORY (tests and siblings add scripts/drivers to sys.path and import 'base' by basename), and scripts/drivers/base.py also shows up in `graph stats`' Orphans list.
B. SAME CAUSE, COVERAGE SURFACE. `hilo graph untested` lists 61 files; 3 of them ARE imported by the repo's own tests: tests/test_proxy_driver_hermes.py does `import hermes as h` and tests/test_proxy_developer_role.py does the same (file: scripts/drivers/hermes.py), tests/test_proxy_driver_pi.py does `import pi as pimod`, tests/test_proxy_driver_deepseek_harness.py does `import deepseek_harness as dh` — while edges.jsonl does carry tested_by rows to the bare pkg names (pkg:hermes 4, pkg:pi 2, pkg:deepseek_harness 2, pkg:base 6). So the same basename-vs-path resolution gap makes a covered file read as 'no test coverage'.
WHY IT MATTERS: README's headline promise is blast radius and test coverage; both are silently wrong (not erroring) on a shape that is common outside src-layout Python packages (script collections, driver/plugin dirs, sys.path-manipulating test suites — this repo's own tests do it).

title: [P2] `graph understand` at its documented default budget returns 27 KB with an EMPTY DETAIL tier ('no detail block fits the 14400-char budget'), and `--budget` does not bound the response (1000 -> 27,339 B, 6000 -> 27,340 B)
description:
Dogfood run 46, HEAD 33ce3a24, binary /var/tmp/hermes-cargo-target/release/hilo (build stamp v0.3.0-530-g33ce3a24-dirty, built 2026-10-20T10:32:47Z), corpus fresh local clone of the task-router repo at d643ef4 (730 tracked files / 314 .py), cloned to /tmp/df46-1206/tr, warmed.
TASK used (a real agent ask on that repo): `hilo graph understand 'add a provider health probe that reads provider health state'`.
OBSERVED (hyperfine-free one-shots, /usr/bin/time -p + wc -c):
* default (help says 'Token budget override (default: 6000)') -> 27,340 bytes / 635 lines / 195 ms, and the DETAIL tier reads '## DETAIL' + '(no files in this tier) — no detail block fits the 14400-char budget'. The MAP tier names the right files (provider_health_probe.py, provider_health_dashboard.py, provider_health_summary.py, router_health.py) but is a list of truncated symbol names, so the response contains NO file context at all — the tier that would let an agent act is empty.
* `--budget 1000` -> 27,339 bytes; `--budget 6000` -> 27,340 bytes; `--budget 20000` -> 74,752 bytes (DETAIL appears: 'scripts/provider_health_probe.py [provenance=ast_exact, score=1.00]'); `--budget 60000` -> 170,411 bytes. So (a) the flag does not bound the response anywhere near its stated meaning — 1000 and 6000 are the same output — and (b) the documented default yields an output ~6.8k tokens against a stated 6000-token budget, while the tier that consumes the budget yields nothing.
HOT PATH (read from source, not guessed): hilo-graph/src/signal.rs:2635 `let detail_budget_chars = opts.token_budget * 4 * 60 / 100;` and at :2647 `if used + block.len() > detail_budget_chars && !position_ordered.is_empty() { break; }` — the FIRST candidate block that does not fit breaks the loop, so one oversized block empties the whole tier instead of being truncated or skipped in favour of the next file; :2666 prints the 'no detail block fits' line. The MAP (:~2595) and SIGNATURES tiers emit every matched file with no char accounting, which is why the response overshoots the stated budget before DETAIL is even considered.
Fix direction: truncate-or-skip per block (continue, not break) so an oversized first block cannot empty the tier; account the MAP/SIGNATURES emission against the same token budget; and make `--budget` visibly bound total output.
acceptance: PASS: on a warmed 314-file corpus, default-budget `hilo graph understand '<task>'` emits at least one DETAIL block (file header + body), total output <= the stated budget (6000 tokens, ~24,000 chars), and `--budget 1000` produces strictly less output than `--budget 6000`. When no detail block fits, the message names the skipped file and its block size.
foreman_note: Related but distinct from DF-WARPFS-102/118 (which describe what the tiers CONTENT-select); this one is the budget/empty-tier mechanics at signal.rs:2635/2647. Latent since the tiers were added.

title: [P2] The whole COV coverage chain is unreachable on any consumer repo: `graph surfaces` refuses on a foreign tree and coverage-links / test-classes / rollup then hard-fail (rc=1) pointing at that same command
description:
Dogfood run 46, HEAD 33ce3a24, binary /var/tmp/hermes-cargo-target/release/hilo (build stamp v0.3.0-530-g33ce3a24-dirty, built 2026-10-20T10:32:47Z), corpus fresh local clone of the task-router repo at d643ef4 (730 tracked files / 314 .py), cloned to /tmp/df46-1206/tr (a real consumer repo, not Hilo itself), warmed.
OBSERVED:
* `hilo graph surfaces` -> rc=1, stderr 'error: hilo graph surfaces only inventories the Hilo repository itself; /tmp/df46-1206/tr is not a Hilo workspace' (+ stdout 'scope: foreign ... No target-repo surfaces were derived and nothing was written to .vfs/graph/').
* `hilo graph coverage-links --unlinked` -> rc=1, 0 bytes, 'error: no surface inventory at <repo>/.vfs/graph/surfaces.jsonl — run `hilo graph surfaces` first (COV-1)'.
* `hilo graph test-classes` -> rc=1, same error. `hilo graph rollup` -> rc=1, same error.
So on any repo that is not Hilo, the COV chain is a dead end whose error message instructs the user to run a command that refuses by design: the workaround it names cannot work, and the docs (docs/cli-reference.md:659-668, docs/graph-engine.md:398-409) document the refusal only for `surfaces` — not that it is the mandatory input of three more commands.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROMISE: README's headline ('a pre-built map of every codebase it touches — dependencies, entrypoints, test coverage, blast radius') advertises test coverage. title: [P1] `hilo init` installs its hooks into `core.hooksPath` — a throwaway clone's init mutated the HOST-WIDE shared hooks dir (/home/kara/.hermes/hooks), and the update REPLACED ~109 bytes of prior content with no backup
description:

* `hilo init` printed 'Updated Hilo block in post-commit / Updated Hilo block in post-merge / Installed git hooks: post-commit, post-merge'.
* But the clone's own hook was NOT created: `ls .git/hooks/post-commit` -> No such file or directory. `git rev-parse --git-path hooks/post-commit` -> /home/kara/.hermes/hooks/post-commit, because core.hooksPath is set GLOBALLY on this host (`git config --get core.hooksPath` = /home/kara/.hermes/hooks).

* CONSEQUENCE 1 (blast radius): initialising a THROWAWAY CLONE mutated hook state that EVERY repo on the box reads — including the fleet's gitreins guard chain (/home/kara/.hermes/hooks/pre-commit is the live guard hook for all repos). Any commit, in any repo, now runs hilo's block (`hilo graph warm --changed` on post-commit; `[ -f .vfs/.dirty ] && hilo graph warm` on post-merge) in that repo's tree.
* CONSEQUENCE 2 (destructive + unrecoverable): the update is NOT an append. Stripping hilo's current 149-byte delimited block leaves 301 bytes against the 410-byte pre-tick file, so ~109 bytes of previous hook content were REPLACED, and hilo wrote NO backup (gitreins writes `.bak-<ts>` beside any hook it touches - see the four /home/kara/.hermes/hooks/pre-commit.bak-* files it left). The pre-image is therefore unrecoverable; this finder's own pre-tick snapshot protocol was also too late (a snapshot was taken only after init ran), so the delta is documented, not undone.
* RECURRING, not a one-off: sibling repos on this host still carry an OLDER hilo block variant with an `else` branch that writes `.vfs/.dirty` (crier/.git/hooks/post-commit 295 B, duckbrain/.git/hooks/post-commit 305 B), i.e. init rewrites the block it finds.
* RELATED BUT DISTINCT: DF-WARPFS-83 (pending P1) is about the post-merge block being dead code (nothing writes .vfs/.dirty); this row is about WHERE init installs and what it destroys when core.hooksPath is set. DF-WARPFS-157 (closed) was the shared pre-commit arm; this is the post-commit/post-merge side.
Fix direction: (a) never write outside the target repo - install to <repo>/.git/hooks and, when core.hooksPath resolves elsewhere, print the resolved path and REFUSE (or require an explicit --hooks-path flag); (b) if a hook file must be modified, write a byte-exact backup first (as gitreins does) and say so; (c) make the block idempotent-by-content so an update cannot shrink the file. Remediation disclosure: since a HILO block was already present pre-tick, the current block was LEFT IN PLACE (removing it would change host behaviour more than the update did); snapshots at /tmp/df46-1206/hooks-before/.

ROOT CAUSE — three divergent copies of one policy:
  * hilo-graph/src/audit.rs:315-326 — `const PRUNE_DIRS: [&str; 10]` = [target, node_modules, vendor, __pycache__, venv, .venv, site-packages, .cache, .rustup, .npm]. No "target-local". title: [P2] PERF: cold `hilo graph search` scans 6,622 persisted build-dir paths inherited from graph.db — 30.0s -> 1.66s (18.1x, HEAD release) on warpfs; the symbol corpus at hilo-cli/src/commands/graph.rs:194 filters nothing, and prune.rs cannot remove the immortal `target-local/` endpoints (distinct root cause from PERF-013's audit walker)
reasoning:
PERF hunt 2026-10-27 (perf lane, stand-in workdir /home/kara/.hermes/stand-in/perf/warpfs). Repo HEAD 6b3e8a9e at measurement time (now 8cb3ca2a; sibling lanes land commits continuously on this shared checkout). Corpus: /home/kara/warpfs.

SYMPTOM: the first `hilo graph search <query>` after the symbol cache is invalidated (cold) takes ~30s on a repo with 246 real source files, and its ranking mixes vendored DuckDB C++ build output into the hits. Warm (cache-hit) runs are 0.67s, so the cost is the cold scan, not the query.

EXACT COMMAND (every arm): cd <arm root> && rm -f .vfs/graph/.symbols_cache.json && /usr/bin/time -p <hilo> graph search impact > /dev/null

HEADLINE — HEAD release binary v0.3.0-660-g6b3e8a9e-dirty (built 2026-10-27T17:56Z, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/hermes-cargo-target), arms interleaved A,B,B,A:
ARM A — real state (graph.db carries 36,070 target-local edges; target-local/ present on disk, 20,522 files / 5.9 GB):
  A1 real=30.67s user=27.25s sys=0.38s (load 15.8)   A2 real=29.36s user=28.86s sys=0.29s (load 15.4)
ARM B — IDENTICAL tree (hardlink copy of arm A, target-local/ still on disk) with a FRESHLY warmed graph (corpus 246 paths, 0 build-dir paths):
  B1 real=1.58s user=1.53s sys=0.03s (load 15.8)     B2 real=1.73s user=1.61s sys=0.03s (load 17.1)
RESULT: 30.0s -> 1.66s wall (18.1x), 28.1s -> 1.57s user CPU (17.9x). Within-arm spread is 4% on arm A and 9% on arm B, i.e. the arms do not overlap.

CORROBORATION (same command, same arm construction, other binaries):
  * release v0.3.0-542-gd1f88c75 (2026-10-21, the repo's pre-existing target/release/hilo): A real 43.31s user 28.27s -> B real 2.55s user 1.41s = 17.0x wall / 20.0x CPU.
  * debug v0.3.0-650-g0b2745cc (2026-10-27T11:46Z): A real 219.93s / 89.22s (user 84.24s / 80.49s) -> B real 11.91s / 8.48s (user 6.47s / 6.48s) = 12.6x CPU.
The written symbol-cache artefact drops 5,183,402 B -> 328,743 B (15.8x).

CORPUS (the defect itself; the timing is its shadow): .vfs/graph/.symbols_cache.json holds 6,849 paths, of which 6,622 (96.7%) are under target-local/debug/build/ — 3,632 .cpp + 2,930 .hpp + 52 .cc + 8 .rs from two vendored libduckdb-sys trees (3,307 each) and cranelift-codegen — vs 227 real repo paths. graph.db holds 39,293 edges, 36,070 of them (91.8%) with `from` LIKE 'target-local/%' over 6,622 distinct paths; 0 `target/` endpoints, 332 repo endpoints. strace -f -e trace=openat on one cold run: 7,290 openat calls, 6,622 (90.8%) on target-local/ paths, 583 on real repo sources — the cold scan opens exactly the 6,622 build-dir files it read out of the database.

QUALITY IMPACT (not only speed): the arm-A ranking for the query "impact" places `target-local/debug/build/libduckdb-sys-3bf6b95a1ffedfbe/out/duckdb/src/common/extra_type_info.cpp` among its top hits; build artifacts compete with repo source in the returned result list.

ROOT CAUSE — the symbol corpus inherits PERSISTED build-dir endpoints, and nothing may prune them:
  * hilo-cli/src/commands/graph.rs:194 `symbol_source_paths()` builds the corpus as graph endpoints UNION warm's parse-cache keys with NO component/prune filter. The read+hash+extract loop that owns the ~30s is scan_symbol_sources() at graph.rs:244-331 (open at :260, SHA256 over every byte at :272-288, symbol/doc extraction at :299 / :306).
  * hilo-cli/src/commands/graph.rs:215-232 `symbol_edge_endpoint_paths()` takes GraphDB::distinct_files() and filters only scheme prefixes (pkg:/sys:/local:/std:/external:) and language extension, so a `target-local/....cpp` survives.
  * hilo-graph/src/prune.rs:16-22 — warm prunes only (1) endpoints whose FILE no longer exists and (2) rows superseded by this pass's re-derivation of the same `from`. target-local files DO exist (20,522 files / 5.9 GB) and are never re-derived now that discovery stopped descending into them, so those 36,070 rows are IMMORTAL and the corpus re-materialises on every cold scan.
  * Why they exist at all: hilo-cli/src/commands/guard.rs:34-46 `DEFAULT_PRUNE_DIRS` gained "target-local" only on 2026-10-11 (commit 0056678e), which fixed DISCOVERY; rows written before that date stay in graph.db indefinitely.
  * Four divergent copies of the prune policy now exist: guard.rs:34-46 (HAS target-local), hilo-graph/src/audit.rs:315 (PERF-013, lacks it), hilo-cli/src/commands/coverage_links.rs:444 (lacks it), hilo-graph/src/graph.rs:2952-2978 `NON_COMPONENT_DIRS` (lacks it) — hilo-graph cannot depend on hilo-cli, which is how they drift.
  * RELATION TO PERF-013 (filed 18:18Z today): that row fixes `graph audit`, whose OWN walker reads the tree. `graph search` never walks — it reads graph.db and the parse cache — so adding target-local to audit.rs's PRUNE_DIRS does NOT change this corpus (code-inspected, not measured). Same user-visible class, different root cause and different file:line; PERF-013's "one canonical table" recommendation is the durable half of this one too.

FIX DIRECTION (one change): filter the symbol corpus at graph.rs:194 — drop every relative path whose first component is a build/dependency/cache directory before the scan (the guard table's vocabulary), keeping the DF-WARPFS-116 zero-edge inclusion for real source files. Pin it with a target-local/ fixture in the CLI symbol-cache tests (the temp-repo harness at graph.rs:3750+ already exists). Durable: hoist ONE canonical prune table into hilo-core and consume it from guard, audit, coverage_links AND the symbol corpus; optionally add a third prune rule (non-component path) to prune.rs so existing graph.db junk is reaped by `graph warm`.

VERIFIED WORKAROUND FOR EXISTING CHECKOUTS (no code change): clear the graph state and re-warm in the same tree — corpus 6,849 -> 246 paths, cold search 30.0s -> 1.66s on the HEAD release binary (measured as arm B).

UNVERIFIED / LIMITS OF THIS EVIDENCE:
  1. Arm B is a freshly-warmed-corpus arm, NOT a patched binary: this lane does not edit the target's code. It removes exactly the paths the fix would remove (246 remain), and it is measured on the HEAD release binary, but the foreman must still re-measure with the real patched binary.
  2. No CPU profile: perf is unusable on this host (kernel.perf_event_paranoid=4; `perf record` fails "Failure to open any events for recording") and cargo-flamegraph rides on perf, so cost is attributed by arms + strace openat counts. The split inside the 30s (file read vs SHA256 vs tree-sitter extraction) is NOT measured.
  3. The HEAD release binary is stamped `-dirty` (the shared checkout carried uncommitted sibling changes when it was built) and its build was started before HEAD moved to 8cb3ca2a; it is a HEAD-of-13:00 build, not a pinned-commit artefact.
  4. Host load was 15-36 on 16 cores with sibling lanes (concurrent cargo build/test, a `hilo serve`, other agent ticks); wall times swung 89-220s within the SAME arm at high load (debug profile). USER CPU is the stable metric (28.1s vs 1.57s at the headline; 82.4s vs 6.48s debug).
  5. Arm A's graph.db also holds more edges overall than arm B's freshly built one, so the delta contains a second, smaller database-loading term that was not separately measured; the 6,622 endpoint identity is exact (strace + corpus JSON), the split of the timing is not.
